newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa manufacturers optimistic about year ahead.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa manufacturers optimistic about year ahead.

text.p: Manufacturers are optimistic that sales volumes will improve in the year ahead and the majority expect to utilise more their production capacity as a result, according to the South African Chamber of Business.

In its latest survey of confidence levels in the manufacturing sector, the chamber (Sacob) said 75 percent of those polled in January epected sales to increase in the next 12 months, compared with 70 percent in November last year.
"The upbeat sales outlook has resulted in a stable proportion of manufacturers expecting to utilise more of their production capacity at around 70 percent," the chamber said.

Chamber economist Penny Hawkins said a highlight of the survey was the fact that half of the respondents polled expected to employ more unskilled labour in the next twelve months, which was a new feature of manufacturers expectations.

"Fifty-one percent of respondents said they would employ unskilled labour in the year ahead compared with 41 percent in November," Hawkins said, an increase she attributed to the buoyant sales outlook.
The chamber said that in order to take advantage of the export opportunities presented by the weaker rand, upgrading of plant and equipment might be necessary.

However, the number of respondents that expected to upgrade existing plant and equipment had remained relatively stable and fewer respondents expected to invest in new capacity, which the chamber said reflected the influence of higher interest rates.

"This together with the pressures on the balance of payments, underlines the importance of attracting additional capital to South Africa, and of implementing the various investment incentives as a matter of urgency," it said.
